20 goals | biggest home win = | biggest away win = | highest scoring = Malacca 0-9 Perak | matches = 156 | total goals = 480 | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2005–06 Malaysia Super League|2005–06]] | nextseason = [[2007–08 Malaysia Super League|2007–08]] }} The '''2006–07 Liga Super''' ({{langx|en|'''2006–07 Super League'''}}), also known as the '''TM Liga Super''' for sponsorship reasons, was the fourth season of the [[Liga Super]], the top-tier professional [[association football|football]] league in Malaysia.[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay07.html ] 2007 Liga Super The season was held from 16 December 2006 and concluded on 4 August 2007. The [[Liga Super]] champions for 2006–07 was [[Kedah FA|Kedah]]. The [[Football Association of Malaysia|FAM]] has decided to expand the league from eight teams to 14 in total, however, only 13 clubs compete at the start of the season after [[MPPJ F.C.|MPPJ]] pulled from the league. The highest scoring game was between [[Malacca FA|Malacca]] and [[Perak FA|Perak]] where Perak defeat Malacca by 9–0. [[Perak FA|Perak]]'s [[Keita Mandjou]] and [[DPMM FC|DPMM]]'s [[Mohd Shahrazen Said]] were joint-top scorer with 21 goals each. [[Kedah FA|Kedah]]'s [[Marlon Alex James]] was in third place with 20 goals. ==Team changes== The following teams have changed division. {{col-begin|width=auto}} {{col-break}} ===To Malaysia Super
